findings.title: LEFT JOIN omits date/month filter on expenses
findings.description: The new query joins expenses to budgets only on user_id and category, with no condition tying e.spent_on to the requested `month`. This aggregates a category's spend across all time instead of just the target month, unlike the original monthly_summary() which scoped expenses to the month. Budget status will report inflated 'spent'/'remaining'/'over_budget' values for any user with expenses in that category from other months, despite the PR claiming 'no behavior change'.

No test was added/updated to verify budget_status only counts expenses within the given month for a category that also has expenses in other months. Such a test would have caught the missing month filter in the new JOIN query.
findings.title: Missing regression test for month-scoped spend aggregation
CREATE INDEX not idempotent, breaks reopening existing database
findings.description: SCHEMA is executed via executescript() every time DB() is constructed, implying the DDL must be safe to re-run against an already-initialized database file (the existing CREATE TABLE statements presumably use IF NOT EXISTS for this reason). The new `CREATE INDEX idx_expenses_user_category ...` has no IF NOT EXISTS clause, so opening the DB a second time against an existing file (e.g. app restart) will raise sqlite3.OperationalError: index already exists.

findings.title: synchronous=OFF risks database corruption on crash/power loss
findings.description: Setting PRAGMA synchronous = OFF disables fsync at critical points; on an OS crash or power loss (not just an application crash) the database file can become corrupted, and recent committed transactions can be lost. For a financial/expense-tracking application this is a significant durability regression introduced purely for write speed, without at least using WAL mode + synchronous=NORMAL, which offers a much safer speed/durability tradeoff.
